content.text: Let me look at how the post list and the save mutation are wired before changing anything.
The save mutation only writes the detail cache. Let me see how publish handles the same list, since the symptom says publish already updates the list correctly.

That confirms it: nothing invalidates or refetches the post list's own cached query after a draft save succeeds, so the list keeps serving what it fetched before the edit until something unrelated happens to refetch it. Publish already invalidates both the list and the detail; save only ever wrote the detail. This is a TanStack Query cache-invalidation gap, so let me check that skill for the right way to add it without disturbing the existing detail write.

content.text: Fixed. getPostSaveMutationOptions only ever wrote the post's own detail cache on success, and nothing invalidated or refetched the site's post list query, so the list kept showing its old title and timestamp until some unrelated navigation happened to refetch it. Publish already had this right — it invalidates both the list and the detail — save did not. I added an invalidateQueries call for the post list's own query key (from getPostListQueryOptions) alongside the existing setQueryData for the detail, so a save now updates both the same way a publish already does. The existing unit tests, lint, and format checks all pass with no other changes.
